findings.F1: The test's own result is on the side the idea predicts but short of the bar: the short cases' mean unusual 5-day move is +0.91 % with t 1.70 over 487 cases on 377 days, and the strong-minus-weak check passed at +0.59 %. The effect is real-signed but too small for this sample to show clearly, and the data holds 13 more coins than the six tested.
findings.F2: In folds B and C, the same cases give a mean unusual move that grows with the horizon: +0.70 % at 5 days (t 0.83, 315 cases, 195 days), +1.63 % at 10 days (t 1.34, 306 cases) and +4.74 % at 20 days (t 2.31, 274 cases, 172 days). The plan's 5-day horizon reads the drift where it is still small against a usual 5-day move of 10.60 %.
findings.F3: In falling markets in folds B and C, shrunk volume behaves differently from grown volume at 5 days: +1.86 % after shrunk volume (t 1.33, 218 cases) against −1.10 % after grown volume (t −0.64, 183 cases). The most-shrunk third gives +3.95 % (t 1.90, 73 cases) against +0.31 % to +1.29 % for the other two thirds, as the brief's dry-up claim expects.

ideas.name: dry-up moderate declines, all coins
ideas.idea: In a falling market, the more a coin's trading volume over the past 30 days has shrunk against the 30 days before, the larger its fall over the next 5 days, and more so the more moderate its 20-day fall has been, the continuation fading as the 20-day fall turns into a plunge.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts a quiet, moderate decline and stays out of a dried-up coin that has just plunged, where the sellers are already exhausted.
